metaDescription: The volunteer board that governs Asian Doula Alliance: its directors, how ADA’s certified doulas elect it, and its conflict of interest rules.
electionMetaDescription: How ADA’s certified doulas nominate and elect the board of directors, who can stand for election, and how to nominate.
title: Board of directors and elections
lead: A volunteer board governs ADA. It sets ADA’s direction, oversees its finances and holds ADA to its mission.
meta: The board of {legalName}, which does business as {dba}.

cta.title: Certified doulas in good standing can nominate a director.

composition.payValue: Directors are volunteers and receive no compensation from ADA.

boardSection.title: The board
boardSection.intro: The board’s {count} volunteer directors set ADA’s certification standards and steward the nonprofit, without compensation.

qiWang.bio: Doula and doula educator. Qi Wang seeded what would become the Asian Doula Alliance in {year}, starting from a WeChat community of Asian-immigrant postpartum caregivers and growing it into the seed of a national professional body. Her conviction, that culturally integrated postpartum care deserved both the dignity of formal certification and a community that protected the women practicing it, remains ADA’s founding premise. As Founder Emeritus, she advises on community and cultural fidelity as ADA grows beyond its founding roots.

sethMeng.bio: Seth Meng was elected ADA’s inaugural Board President at the {year} board meeting, where he serves as the executive lead for technology, governance and standards. His background is as an analyst and researcher in elder-care outcomes at the University of Rochester Medical Center, applying statistics and machine learning to questions of long-term care quality and family-caregiver impact. That orientation toward measurement, instrumentation and protective system design now shapes ADA’s certification platform, multilingual exam architecture and public verification registry. Seth came to ADA out of a long-standing commitment to building public-benefit institutions.

wesleyLau.bio: Wesley Lau is a serial entrepreneur and venture capital investor whose career has crossed several industries, from technology and finance to community-focused initiatives. Outside his professional work, he has been a steady presence in community and public-benefit organizations, drawn to neighborhood cleanups and the unglamorous volunteer work others overlook. He brings that same orientation to ADA’s board: that good organizations are built by people who do the small, repeatable work as carefully as the strategic decisions.

minyuZhang.bio: Minyu Zhang spent her earlier career in finance before turning much of her time and energy toward public-benefit work. She volunteers across a range of community and nonprofit initiatives, with a particular commitment to animal welfare and rescue. On ADA’s board, she pairs financial discipline with steady engagement in mission-driven organizations, reading budgets carefully and showing up for the work because she cares about the people behind it.

veronicaTseng.bio: Veronica Tseng works in postpartum doula service operations across the Bay Area, Southern California, Seattle, New York City and Chicago, where she focuses on doula coordination and family-facing program delivery. She brings that ground-level view to ADA’s board, informing conversations on member needs, program quality, and how certification standards translate into daily practice for the doulas and families ADA serves.

miaLiu.bio: Mia Liu leads operations for a doula services organization, overseeing doula workforce coordination, regional service delivery and the day-to-day work of running culturally integrated postpartum care at scale. She brings to ADA’s board the practical realities of the field: the regional service markets, the doulas who carry the work, and the families they serve. She helps the board calibrate certification standards against operational reality.

election.title: How elections work
election.intro: ADA’s certified doula community elects the board. Directors serve terms of {years} years.
election.step1Body: Any ADA-certified doula in good standing can nominate themselves or a colleague. A nominee must have held an active certification for at least {months} months, and must confirm that they are willing to serve.
election.step2Body: The board reviews every nomination to confirm eligibility. Candidates are told the result and asked for a short candidate statement.
election.step3Body: Certified doulas with active status vote by electronic ballot, one vote per position. The results are tallied independently.
election.step4Body: ADA announces the newly elected directors, and their term begins. Outgoing directors support a handover of {days} days.
election.certificationValue: An active ADA certification, held for at least {months} months.
election.standingValue: In good standing, with no active disciplinary action.
election.commitmentValue: Serve a full term of {years} years and attend at least {percent}% of the quarterly board meetings.
election.termValue: Each term is {years} years. There are no term limits, so directors may stand again.
election.nominateBody: Email <mail></mail> with the subject line “{subject}” and a short statement of intent. ADA accepts nominations year-round.

conflicts.title: Conflicts of interest
conflicts.everyYearValue: Each director signs a conflict of interest disclosure.
conflicts.abstainingValue: A director with a material interest in a decision abstains and does not vote on it.
conflicts.relatedPartiesValue: A related-party transaction needs the affirmative vote of the independent directors.
conflicts.policyValue: A written conflict of interest policy, reviewed every year. A copy is available on request from <mail></mail>.
conflicts.accountabilityValue: ADA files a public {form990} every year, starting with fiscal year {year}.
